title: The tensor product of quasi-coherent modules is quasi-coherent, with sections over affine opens the tensor product of sections
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $\mathcal F,\mathcal G$ quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-modules [pqf-def-coherent], [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Let $\mathcal F\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}\mathcal G$ be their tensor product [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], the sheafification of the presheaf $U\mapsto\mathcal F(U)\otimes_{\mathcal O_X(U)}\mathcal G(U)$, and $t_U:\mathcal F(U)\otimes_{\mathcal O_X(U)}\mathcal G(U)\to(\mathcal F\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}\mathcal G)(U)$ the component of the sheafification map. Then $\mathcal F\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}\mathcal G$ is quasi-coherent, and for every affine open $U\subseteq X$ the $\mathcal O_X(U)$-linear map $t_U$ is bijective.

source.place: Schemes, Lemma 01I8 (lemma-widetilde-constructions, line 1113, item (1): (M (x)_R N)~ = M~ (x)_{O_X} N~ on X = Spec R) and Section 01LA (section-quasi-coherent, line 4717, item (8)); Modules, Lemma 01CE (modules.tex line 2440, lemma-tensor-product-permanence (3))

proof.text: Fix an affine open $U\subseteq X$, write $R=\mathcal O_X(U)$, and identify $U\cong\operatorname{Spec}R$ by the canonical affine chart. Restricting a quasi-coherent module to this affine open remains quasi-coherent, and the affine tilde/global-sections equivalence identifies $\mathcal F|_U$ with $\widetilde{\mathcal F(U)}$ and $\mathcal G|_U$ with $\widetilde{\mathcal G(U)}$.

source.place: Schemes, Section 01LA item (1), Lemmas 01IA and 01IB; restriction to an affine open

proof.text: On $U=\operatorname{Spec}R$, apply the affine tilde-tensor comparison to $M=\mathcal F(U)$ and $N=\mathcal G(U)$. The sectionwise tensor presheaf restricts to the corresponding tensor presheaf on $U$ by definition. For sheafification, let $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ be the open immersion and let $P$ be this tensor presheaf on $X$, with sheafification $P^\#$. For every sheaf $H$ of $\mathcal O_U$-modules, the four Hom sets are naturally identified: $\operatorname{Hom}_U((P^\#)|_U,H)=\operatorname{Hom}_X(P^\#,j_*H)=\operatorname{Hom}_X(P,j_*H)=\operatorname{Hom}_U(P|_U,H)$. The first and last equalities use [lem-weil-pbc-module-restriction-open-immersion-colimits], which says restriction is left adjoint to direct image; the middle equality is the sheafification universal property [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification]; and $j_*H$ is a sheaf by [lem-weil-pbc-site-continuous-pushforward-sheaf], with the open-immersion direct image as in [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. Thus $(P^\#)|_U$ is canonically the sheafification of $P|_U$, so $(\mathcal F\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}\mathcal G)|_U\cong(\mathcal F|_U)\otimes_{\mathcal O_U}(\mathcal G|_U)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-tensor] this is canonically $\widetilde{M\otimes_RN}$, with $m\otimes n$ sent to $\tau_M(m)\otimes\tau_N(n)$. Therefore the original component $t_U:M\otimes_RN\to(\mathcal F\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}\mathcal G)(U)$ is the affine node's global-sections bijection.

source.place: Schemes, Lemma 01I8 item (1); Modules, Lemma 01CE item (3), with restriction and sheafification expanded from their definitions

proof.text: By [pqf-def-coherent], an $\mathcal O_X$-module is quasi-coherent when every point has an affine open neighbourhood on which it is isomorphic to $\widetilde P$ for some module $P$. Every point of the scheme $X$ has an affine open neighbourhood [def-pc-scheme], and Step 2 identifies the tensor product on each such $U$ with $\widetilde{\mathcal F(U)\otimes_{\mathcal O_X(U)}\mathcal G(U)}$. Thus the tensor product is quasi-coherent. Step 2 also proves the asserted bijectivity of $t_U$ for every affine open $U$.
